- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast, particularly if recent price action shows upward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5-10 days; apply downward correction of 1-3% to avoid overreaction.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion bias — reduce forecast by 1-2% for next 3-5 days unless sentiment strongly supports.
- If sentiment history shows multiple 0.00 or low values (≤0.3), model tends to lag; adjust forecast upward by 0.5-1.5% to catch momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds model by >5% in 3-5 days, model may be underestimating trend — increase forecast by 0.5-1.5% for next 5-7 days if sentiment remains bullish.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3 days, model often misses the turn — adjust forecast upward by 1-2% in next 3-5 days.
